operation_bindings.query_signature: Input: $a_t\in[K],\quad t\le\tau_\delta$. The specification's protocol governs timing and visible information.

comparators.definition: True best arm $b(\mu)$, rather than a comparator defined by cumulative realized rewards

norms.definition: The model specifies coordinate ranges of finite vectors. Discrete action labels have no derivative order. A placeholder norm imposes no additional geometric assumption.

objects.definition: Arms have distributions $\nu_i=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\mu_i)$, with $\mu\in(0,1)^K$ and unique best arm $b(\mu)$. The parameters $K$ and $\delta$ are public. The algorithm must be $\delta$-correct and stop almost surely on every admissible instance. Compare expected sample count at a fixed $\mu$.
The mean μ_i belongs to the ith fixed reward distribution. It is unknown and cannot be queried directly.

protocols.adversary_information: The unknown distribution or parameter is fixed before interaction. Learner randomness and sample randomness are independent. No adversary changes the distribution round by round from the learner's history.
protocols.loss_bearing_points: There is no online regret loss. Each arm pull contributes only to the sampling cost τδ.
protocols.past_requery: No new information may be requested from past rounds or previously used samples. Received feedback may be stored and processed. In a stochastic model, an action may be repeated in a new round, with a fresh charged sample.
protocols.queries_per_round: One sample per call, with random total tau_delta; the primary resource is E_mu[tau_delta].
steps: The environment fixes $\mu$. The values $K,\delta$ and the Bernoulli family are public.
Use the history to decide whether to continue; if continuing, select an arm before drawing one fresh sample.
The recommendation is returned at the history-dependent stopping time $\tau_\delta$.
Require error probability at most delta and almost-surely finite tau_delta for every admissible mu.
